artifacts.summary: Settles the state.json batch-entry schema shape, the per-section authored/generated ruling for ROADMAP.md's six non-batch sections, the write-path answer (state-write.sh + edge_only), and task 313's disposition (superseded parse layer, not edited).

memory_candidates.content: In this codebase's state.json writer (state-write.sh), the audit-evidence gate (--audit-verdict/--audit-override) fires ONLY when a write's jq transform introduces a genuinely new active_projects project_number. Every other write -- status updates, artifact links, file_scope edits, and any non-active_projects top-level field (e.g. a new roadmap_batches array) -- is byte-for-byte unaffected by the gate. A new feature that edits existing task fields or adds a sibling top-level array never needs audit plumbing.

When a system already has a per-item enum field for one axis (e.g. a task's own critical/high/medium/low priority, written by a severity mapping) and a NEW feature needs a different, group-level ordering axis (e.g. batch run order), avoid manufacturing a second priority-shaped field. Use the new entry's own array position as its ordinal -- the same way a hand-authored ordered list's line order already functions as its priority signal before any schema existed. This avoids a 'third unused axis' when two existing fields already disagree on which one should carry ordering.
